When the verse against raising voices above the Prophet's came, loud-voiced Thabit b. Qais stayed home thinking himself of the Fire, but the Prophet said he was of Paradise.
At a garden well the Prophet had Abu Musa admit Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman with glad tidings of Paradise, Uthman's coming with a trial he would face.
Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas guarded the Prophet at night, was offered the Prophet's parents as ransom at Uhud, had verses revealed about him, and with Talha stayed by the Prophet.
At the Battle of the Trench the Prophet called Zubair his helper, as every prophet has one, and offered him his father and mother as ransom.
When Hira stirred, the Prophet told it only a prophet, a truthful one and a martyr were on it; Aisha said Abu Bakr and Zubair answered Allah's call after misfortune.
The Prophet called Abu Ubaida b. Jarrah this Umma's man of trust, before Yemenis seeking a teacher, and sent him to Najran's people, who asked for a trustworthy man.
Zaid b. Haritha was called son of Muhammad until a verse said to name people after their fathers; the Prophet defended Usama's and Zaid's command, both among his dearest.
Abdullah b. Ja'far recalled the Prophet mounting him and Fatima's sons on his beast on returning from journeys, and telling him a secret he would tell no one.
The Prophet visited Umm Aiman, who was annoyed when he declined her drink; after his death Abu Bakr and Umar visited her and wept with her that revelation had ceased.
The Prophet visited Umm Sulaim, whose brother was killed with him; he heard her and Bilal's steps in Paradise and blessed her and Abu Talha after their son's death.
The Prophet counted Ibn Mas'ud among the believers of verse 5:93; Abu Musa took him for one of the Prophet's household, and Abu Mas'ud knew no one left more learned.
The Prophet said the Throne of the Most Compassionate shook at Sa'd b. Mu'adh's death, and that his kerchiefs in Paradise were better than a silk garment people admired.
Abu Dharr came to Mecca to find the Prophet, lived on Zamzam water, embraced Islam, proclaimed it aloud and was beaten, and half of his tribe Ghifar then accepted Islam.
Since Jarir embraced Islam the Prophet never refused to see him and always smiled at him, and prayed that he be firm on horseback and rightly guided.
Ibn Abbas placed water for the Prophet's ablution, and the Prophet prayed that Allah grant him deep understanding of religion.
Ibn Umar dreamt a silk cloth flew wherever he aimed in Paradise and angels took him to the Fire; the Prophet called him pious and wished he prayed at night.
Umm Sulaim brought Anas to serve the Prophet, who prayed for increase in his wealth and children, and Anas kept a secret the Prophet told him, even from his mother.
The Prophet said Abdullah b. Salam was in Paradise and explained his dream of climbing a pillar to a handhold as holding fast to Islam until death.
After the Prophet prayed, Abu Huraira's mother accepted Islam; Abu Huraira says he narrates much because he stayed with the Prophet and never forgot, and Aisha faulted his hasty narrating.
The Prophet gave Abu Musa and Bilal glad tidings a Bedouin refused, prayed forgiveness for Abu Amir and Abu Musa, and praised the Ash'arites' night recitation and food-sharing.
Abu Sufyan asked the Prophet to marry his daughter Umm Habiba, take Mu'awiya as scribe and make him a commander against the unbelievers, and the Prophet agreed to all three.
When Abu Bakr rebuked Salman, Suhaib and Bilal for their words about Abu Sufyan, the Prophet said annoying them would annoy his Lord, and Abu Bakr apologised to them.
The Prophet said he safeguards his Companions and they his community, and armies will win having among them one who saw him, or saw those who saw him.
The Prophet said the best people are his generation, then the next, then the next, after whom come people who testify unasked, break vows, are untrustworthy and grow fat.
The Prophet forbade reviling his Companions, saying others spending gold as much as Uhud would not equal a mudd of theirs, after Khalid b. Walid reviled Abd al-Rahman b. Awf.
Ibn Umar praised the dead Abdullah b. Zubair hanging by the road; his mother Asma told Hajjaj he had ruined his own Hereafter and was the foretold murderer of Thaqif.
Sa'd, the first Arab to shoot an arrow in Allah's cause, recalled having only tree leaves to eat with the Prophet, and protested that Banu Asad instructed him in religion.
Aisha told Urwa that Muslims were commanded to ask forgiveness for the Prophet's companions, but they reviled them instead.
